curve.comment: I kind of like 1, but it's a bit too shaky instead of glitchy if that makes sense. It should have more of that text glitch effect we use when updating a live value, make a couple of variations on that
curve.reply: Option 1 stays as the reference. Four new options play the live-update stutter on the whole part instead of shaking it: two copies (yellow right and up, cyan right and down) come home 6, 4, 2 and 1 px in four ticks over 480 ms (converge, slice, tear, split). Converge is recommended.

opening.comment: power flicker seems best out of those, but one thing I don't like is that I have these corners that have an edge sometimes, but when the animation comes around, it draws a rectange around that and the corners are square again. So give me 5 alternatives on this one, make it aligned with the ones that I commissioned for the earlier step
opening.reply: Fixed: the animations clipped the part with a plain rectangle and only the last frame put the notch back; the notch is now cut at every frame (checked on power flicker). Power flicker stays, plus glitched in and five alternatives in the same stutter language as the motion curve: converge, blink, slice, tear, split. Every close is still its open reversed.

spinner.comment: signal bars are best, give me a couple variations, maybe slow it a tad down, it's a bit too jumpy atm
spinner.reply: Signal bars are about a fifth as jumpy: one bar steps at a time, 240 ms a step instead of 120 ms (a loop is 2.4 s instead of 1.8 s). Five variations beside them: a rising meter, a glitching copy, a peak-hold tick, an equaliser from a centre line and a skyline with a travelling light.

leave.comment: glitched in is best, but make new variations based on the ones I commissioned in step 1 and 2
leave.reply: Torn out, glitched in stays first. Six new pairs are built from the motion-curve and opening ideas: converge, blink, flicker, slice, tear and split. Every exit is its arrival reversed, measured frame by frame, and the notched corners stay cut at every frame.

hover.comment: I like split edge, but in menu, the right square edge goes beyond the edge of the corner of the menu itself, can we fix that? give me a couple of variations, let's say five, and five that are glitchy
hover.reply: Fixed: the doubled edge now follows the part's own cut at every frame (the menu entry follows the menu's notch), so nothing sticks out at the corner. Split edge stays first; ten more: five variations of the doubled edge (end bar, double rule, closing half frame, staggered bars, swapped colours) and five glitchy ones (flash and split, jitter, slice, slit, beam). Enter and leave are exact mirrors.
